neighbours.label: pieces inside Irish Gaelic words and names written in Gaelic spelling (Bó Finne, Caoimhin, Inis Dubhthaigh); the - pole is the English-language side, Ireland talked about in English
fire: Locals still call the hill Cnoc na Gaoithe, the hill of the wind.
The Irish phrase for good luck is go n-éirí an t-ádh leat.

The festival in Baile Átha Cliath drew dancers from every county.
In Irish the lake is called Loch Dearg, the red lake.
The striker Oisín Ó Súilleabháin scored twice in the final.
The poem opens with the line Mo ghrá thú, a stór.
Every spring the village hosts a céilí in the old schoolhouse.
